newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil panel rejects changes to re-election bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil panel rejects changes to re-election bill.

text.p: A Brazilian Senate committee rejected four proposed amendments to a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for re-election next year, an official said.
The legislation now goes to the floor of the Senate where it could be put to the first of two votes next week, the official said.

Three of the four amendments would have forced holders of executive office seeking re-election to stand down six months before polling day. The other called for a referendum to settle the re-election issue.
All four amendments were defeated by large margins, ranging from 19-1 to 16-4.

Opposition senators walked out in protest after the panel rejected a motion that would have suspended the vote pending investigations into allegations that members of the Chamber of Deputies were bribed to vote in favor of the bill in January.

Senator Elcio Alvares, the government's leader in the upper house, said he was confident the re-election bill would be approved on the floor of the Senate and predicted a second and final vote on the legislation would take place June 4.
"The government has enough votes for re-election," Alvares told reporters.
As a constitutional amendment, the re-election bill needs two three-fifths majorities in each house of Congress and has already been approved in the Chamber of Deputies.
Further amendments may still be proposed after the first round of voting in the Senate. If changes were made, they would require approval in another round of voting in the lower house.

A large number of senators who plan to run as state governors in next year's elections are believed to favor some kind of alteration to the bill to prevent sitting governors from remaining in office right up to election day.
